fixes.explanation: Ha, plants DO love sunshine, friend, and I'd never argue with a sunbeam. But verse 5 doesn't say a word about the sun. What it says is that the LORD God had not yet sent rain upon the earth, and there was no man to cultivate the ground. No rain and nobody on the job. That's a bakery with no flour and no baker, and I know that kind of quiet.

Roots! I love the garden thinking, friend. But verse 7 says the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and roots never show up there. Dust. That's the word. I spent years sitting under dust in a drawer, and the LORD God took the same stuff and made a living man out of it. My dust just made me sneeze.

Ooh, careful, friend, this one is true! Verse 9 says, “Out of the ground the LORD God gave growth to every tree that is pleasing to the eye and good for food.” The card just puts it in its own words. Trees that look good AND taste good. That's like a cookie that's pretty AND delicious, and I'm telling you, it's rare.

Careful, friend, this one is true! Verse 24 says, “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife…” It comes right after the man speaks about the woman in verse 23, and then the text says what follows from it. So the statement stands, and True is the answer that fits.
